Read deaths and populations from GENESIS (Destatis) flat files

Source: R/data-genesis.R
mt_read_genesis.Rd

Reads tables of the German Federal Statistical Office in the "flat" CSV format of GENESIS-Online and the regional database (columns time, 1_variable_code, 1_variable_attribute_label, ..., value): deaths (for example table 23211-0002) and populations (for example table 12411-0013, on 31 December).

Usage

mt_read_genesis(deaths, population = NULL, years = NULL)

Arguments

deaths

Path of a flat CSV file with deaths, or a data frame read from one.

population

Path or data frame with populations, or NULL.

years

Optional subset of years of the deaths (populations of the year before are kept for exposures from 31 December populations).

Value

An mt_data object with deaths and populations.

Details

Variables are recognised by their codes: GES (sex), codes starting with ALT (age, German labels such as "unter 1 Jahr", "15 bis unter 20 Jahre", "85 Jahre und mehr", "68-Jaehrige" with umlaut), DLAND, KREISE or REGBEZ (region), codes starting with TODUR (cause of death; the total "Insgesamt" becomes level "all", the other levels are the GENESIS codes, their labels are in attribute "cause_labels"), and DINSG (Germany as a whole, dropped). Other variables are kept as stratum variables named by their code. Values "-" (nothing) are zero; ".", "...", "x" and "/" are missing. Stratum variables that only the population table has (for example regions, when the deaths are national) are summed out of the populations.

The reader makes no analysis decisions: populations stay populations, and the periods are those of the source (the year of the reference date). The next steps are usually mt_as_exposure() with type = "dec31", mt_regroup() with age = "deaths" (single-year populations to the age groups of the deaths), mt_fill_suppressed() and mt_group_levels() (cause groups, with total = "all" for a residual group).

Examples

d <- data.frame(time = 2020, `1_variable_code` = "GES", `1_variable_attribute_label` = "weiblich",
                `2_variable_code` = "ALT027", `2_variable_attribute_label` = "85 Jahre und mehr",
                value = "120", check.names = FALSE)
p <- data.frame(time = c("2019-12-31", "2020-12-31"), `1_variable_code` = "GES",
                `1_variable_attribute_label` = "weiblich", `2_variable_code` = "ALT103",
                `2_variable_attribute_label` = "85 Jahre und mehr", value = c(900, 950),
                check.names = FALSE)
x <- mt_read_genesis(d, p)
x <- mt_as_exposure(x, type = "dec31")
mt_obs(x, "exposure")
#>    stratum    sex  label age_lo age_hi period_lo period_hi value
#>      <int> <char> <char>  <num>  <num>     <num>     <num> <num>
#> 1:       1 female female     85    Inf      2020      2021   925
#>          provenance
#>              <char>
#> 1: population_dec31
